segment: Alaska Native corporations and tribal enterprises
gate: VERIFIED CLAIMS ONLY. Two fact-checker rounds. Nothing outside this file may be cited by any downstream room, the study, the demo or the email.

WHO_THEY_ARE.c: Tyonek Native Corporation is the ANCSA village corporation for the Native Village of Tyonek, a Dena'ina Athabascan (Tebughna) community on the northwest shore of Cook Inlet.
Headquartered at 880 H Street, Suite 210, Anchorage, AK 99501-5131.
Owns and manages more than 200,000 acres of land conveyed under ANCSA in 1971.

Mission, verbatim: 'Tyonek's mission is to profitably manage the Corporation so that Tebughna Shareholders have the opportunity to prosper individually and collectively, as well as with our partners in business'.

Careers page, verbatim: 'Tyonek is an Alaska Native Corporation and our profits support education, health services, and quality-of-life programs for members of the Native Village of Tyonek and our more than 950 shareholders'.
Eight named core values: Tebughna (Land, Tribe, People), Tradition, Pride, Good Health, Trust, Success, Leadership, Knowledge.
Workforce composition, verbatim: 'more than 50% U.S military veterans, 42% women and 33% minority'.

SCALE_AND_SHAPE.c: 2024 gross revenue $341,146,301 on Alaska Business Magazine's 2025 Top 49ers listing. TWO FACT-CHECK ROUNDS READ THE RANK DIFFERENTLY, one as 20 and one as 21, so the rank is UNRESOLVED and must not be cited until someone settles it. Revenue itself verified twice.
The 2025 Top 49ers listing records employees as '1,523 Worldwide | 15 Statewide'. Attribute to the listing whenever used.
Their own capabilities page states Tyonek 'employs more than 1,300 skilled artisans, technicians, and aviation professionals'. Use this for narrative sentences.
210,000 square feet of manufacturing space across eight buildings in Madison AL, Huntsville AL and Warner Robins GA.

USASpending lists 22 child recipient registrations under the single parent UEI FM96SF3VF8H9. Near-duplicate entity names are registered separately by state, including FOUR beginning 'TFAB Ground Systems' (one AK, two AL, one GA) and THREE 'Tyonek Engineering & Agile Manufacturing' (GA, AL, AK).
Two FAA-certificated 14 CFR Part 145 Repair Stations, 4SXR048C in Kiln Mississippi and 7TYR728D in Huntsville Alabama. NEITHER IS IN ALASKA.

WHAT_THEY_DO.c: Capabilities page names the customer set, verbatim: 'supporting fixed-wing and rotary-wing platforms for all four military services, U.S. Coast Guard, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and USDA customers'.
Certifications, verbatim: 'Our facilities and operations are certified to ISO 9001:2015, AS9100, AS9110, and DCMA 8210.1C standards'.
The Stennis facility holds ISO 9001:2015, AS9100 Rev D, AS9110 Rev C and FAA Part 145 certificate 4SXR048C.
Tyonek Services Overhaul Facility-Stennis, Tyonek Technical Services, Tyonek Aircraft Overhaul and Tyonek Technical Innovations 'are SBA-Certified 8(a) Companies'.

Tyonek Technical Services won FA8773-25-C-0001, a $98,115,620 firm-fixed-price level-of-effort 8(a) sole-source award from the Acquisition Management and Integration Center Detachment 2 at Tinker AFB, for Cyber Operations Formal Training Support for the 39th Information Operations Squadron, completing February 28 2027.

Tyonek Aircraft Overhaul LLC won a Coast Guard IDIQ with a $16.8M ceiling and a $3.6M base-year order for voice and flight data recorder replacement on MH-65E and MH-60T aircraft, announced October 10 2024.
Tyonek Services Group purchased a 68,000 square foot Huntsville hangar in January 2024, having leased it since 2018. Reported January 23 2024. Do not assert a specific day.

Leadership named on the about page: Stephen Peskosky (CEO), Paul Stein (President, Tyonek Services Group, Inc), Todd White (President, Tyonek Manufacturing Group, Inc), Jason Holmes (Director of IT), Stephanie Deemer (Director of Marketing and Communications).

Additional leadership named on the about page under Senior Management: Joe Webb, Vice President, Business Development; Bethany Basinger, Chief Financial Officer; Connie Downing, Chief Administrative Officer; Heather Hudson, General Counsel; Tina Bruce, Vice President, Human Resources. ADDED LATE: the showrunner built the first claims file carrying only the five names relevant to the buyer question and omitted the rest, which let a study sentence assert that no business development leader appeared in Tyonek's public materials. Joe Webb was independently confirmed on the live about page by the company-analyst, the people-finder and a fact-checker round.

THE_GAO_DECISION.c: GAO decision B-424364, B-424364.2. Protester Tyonek Technical Innovations, LLC of Anchorage, Alaska. Agency Department of the Air Force. RFP No. FA8773-25-R-0002 for cyber operations training support services, issued May 19 2025 as an 8(a) small business set-aside under FAR subpart 15.3.

HARD LIMIT ON THIS FINDING, DO NOT OVERSTATE IT. 'The protest is dismissed.' GAO did NOT reach the merits and decided NOTHING about the quality of Tyonek's past performance. Ground one, untimeliness, because 'the plain language of the solicitation made it unambiguously clear how the agency intended to treat the past performance information of affiliated companies'. Ground two, prematurity, because the challenge 'essentially challenges the agency's evaluation judgments before the award decision has been made'. GAO states 'Tyonek remains in the competition and the agency has not made a final selection decision for award'. Any sentence implying Tyonek lost, was downgraded or was found deficient is FALSE.

The solicitation's affiliate past-performance provision, quoted as the full contiguous block because the first three sentences carry the qualifier that affiliate performance IS considered when documented: 'Affiliate companies, sister companies, teaming arrangements, joint venture agreement, etc., will be considered, provided that sufficient documentation is included in the proposal. The prime contractor must demonstrate that the affiliate will perform significant and critical aspects of the contract if awarded. Proposal documentation should include a copy of the signed arrangement such as documented affiliation, a copy of the teaming agreement, a copy of the joint venture agreement, etc. If the required information is not included in the proposal, the proposed affiliate companies, sister companies, joint venture companies, etc. shall not be evaluated or considered.'

THE_PAPERWORK_SURFACE.c: Mechanical Quality Inspector II posting, Madison AL, live as of 04-Aug-2026, lists among duties, verbatim: 'Complete non-conformance reports as required' and 'Complete AS9102 FAI reports'.

Government Property Analyst posting, Madison AL, posted 14-Jul-2026, requires verbatim 'Working knowledge of FAR Part 45, DFARS 252, DCMA Government Property Management requirements.' It covers government-furnished and contractor-acquired property across the lifecycle, inventories, audits, government reporting and contract closeout.

Faculty Developer - Journeyman posting, San Antonio TX, posted 15-Jul-2026, verbatim: 'Produce comprehensive instructional materials, including training manuals, Plans of Instruction (POIs), syllabi, visual aids, and laboratory guides.'
The corporate job board states verbatim 'Displaying 50 listing(s) that fit your search criteria.' The 50 listings span 12 states, and EXACTLY ONE is in Alaska (Aviation Safety Manager, Anchorage).

WHAT_THE_LAW_REQUIRES.c: 14 CFR 145.213(d), verbatim: 'Except for individuals employed by a repair station located outside the United States, only an employee appropriately certificated as a mechanic or repairman under part 65 is authorized to sign off on final inspections and maintenance releases for the repair station.'

14 CFR 43.9(a)(4), verbatim: 'the signature, certificate number, and kind of certificate held by the person approving the work. The signature constitutes the approval for return to service only for the work performed.'

22 CFR 120.54(b)(1), the ITAR end-to-end encryption carve-out, requires 'the data is not in an unencrypted form' between originator and intended recipient and that 'The means of decryption are not provided to any third party.'

DFARS 252.204-7012 requires external cloud services handling covered defense information to meet FedRAMP Moderate equivalent security requirements, requires implementation of NIST SP 800-171, defines rapid reporting as 'within 72 hours of discovery of any cyber incident', and flows down to subcontractors.

WHAT_THE_EVIDENCE_SAYS_ABOUT_AI_HERE.c: FAA estimate, quoted exactly as written and scoped as written: 'estimates the total annual burden on the international repair station community to be 240,869 hours costing $11,507,548 annually.' THIS IS AN INDUSTRY-WIDE ANNUAL TOTAL, not a per-company figure and not Tyonek's. Never place it beside Tyonek's two repair stations in a way implying their scale, and never render 'the international repair station community' as 'all US repair stations'.

ARSA, verbatim: 'Considering all recordkeeping requirements and not just completion of an application on FAA From 8310-3 resulted in a 23,000 percent increase in hours and a 2,600 percent increase in estimated cost'. This is a change in the FAA's OWN ESTIMATING METHODOLOGY between two Federal Register notices, and it is ARSA's characterization. The burden did NOT rise 23,000 percent. Any sentence implying an exploding compliance burden is FALSE.

GAO, verbatim: 'the examples are from limited experience, and the military services generally lack metrics to evaluate the results of predictive maintenance', and 'they do not replace parts or components regularly based on predictive maintenance forecasts'.

DoD Office of Inspector General found 'the Defense Department did not fully implement predictive maintenance on any existing weapon system', naming 'a lack of quality data' and 'a lack of appropriate workforce skillsets, such as data analysts' as blockers.

Oliver Wyman surveyed 'more than 150 aviation professionals from around the world' and reports verbatim: 'Both this year and last, 58% of respondents reported their companies were stuck at the experimental stage of AI development.' The article separately says organizations 'may need additional investment in data infrastructure and governance', which is forward-looking and must not be restated as the cause of the 58 percent.

GAO on the F-35 ALIS, verbatim: 'critical data in ALIS is often inaccurate or missing', and 'when key data used to assess an aircraft's safety has to be tracked using Excel spreadsheets, there is a chance that something critical could get overlooked.'
McKinsey, verbatim: 'gen AI platforms won't be flawless, and thus airlines and MRO providers should not blindly rely on them in critical scenarios' and 'Humans are always in the driver's seat.'
EASA's AI Concept Paper Issue 2 page describes guidance for Level 1 AI (human assistance) and Level 2 AI (human-AI teaming under human oversight). Do not assert what the paper omits.

THE_FIELD_AROUND_THEM.c: Tyonek's own capabilities page lists machining, inspection, manufacturing space, aircraft bays and FAA Part 145 stations, and contains no mention of AI, artificial intelligence, machine learning, predictive maintenance, automation or data analytics. Absence confirmed on two independent fetches.

Yulista, an Alaska Native Corporation aerospace and defense holding company, publishes a named AI service portfolio including verbatim 'AI Infrastructure Design & Deployment', 'Local and Cloud Model Hosting' and 'End-User Enablement and AI Adoption'. It is positioned as an IT service sold to customers, and nothing on the page claims AI applied inside Yulista's own MRO operations.

Yulista Support Services 'has been awarded a potential five-year, $219.4 million contract' from the U.S. Army for engineering, sensor integration, flight test and aircraft maintenance support, as a total 8(a) small business set-aside. Reported July 11 2024. Do not call it an IDIQ, the article does not.

Amentum, verbatim, on its Army aviation capability page: 'To improve quality and cost effectiveness, Amentum has introduced technological innovations including augmented reality and artificial intelligence.'

V2X, full sentence restored because the omitted clause makes their position STRONGER: 'V2X operationalizes massive volumes of maintenance and logistics data using advanced data analytics, Agenetic Model Management, and data visualization to bring predictive maintenance to our customers.' It also markets AMMO, 'Aircraft Maintenance and Management Optimization', a 'real-time, integrated platform', and states it provides 'a secure, AI-ready cloud foundation'. The page has a section headed Predictive Maintenance.

Akima's aviation capability page names no AI, artificial intelligence, machine learning, predictive maintenance, analytics or automation anywhere, including nav and footer. Absence confirmed on two fetches. Scoped to THIS PAGE only.

M1 Support Services states 5,000+ employees and 570+ aircraft platforms supported. Its HOMEPAGE names no AI, machine learning, predictive maintenance or analytics. Scoped to the homepage, not the whole site.

Chugach Government Solutions' homepage names nine capability areas: Audio Visual, C5ISR, Cybersecurity, Engineering, Enterprise IT & Sustainment, IT Accreditation & Certifications, IT Infrastructure, Manufacturing, and System Integration & Install. That page names no AI, machine learning, automation or analytics. Scoped to the homepage.

CONTACT.router_note: She is a ROUTER, not the buyer, and she sits at the Alabama operating campus, not Anchorage. The email must be written to be forwarded and must not assume she is local.
CONTACT.buyer_note: Stephen Peskosky (CEO) owns the enterprise decision. Paul Stein (President, Tyonek Services Group) and Todd White (President, Tyonek Manufacturing Group) own the operating P&Ls. Jason Holmes is Director of IT. No personal email for any of them exists in clear anywhere fetched, and none was constructed.

ADJUDICATED_CONFLICTS.acreage: USE 'more than 200,000 acres' and cite tyonek.com/alaska-operations. Do not cite the Top 49ers 190,000 alongside it.
ADJUDICATED_CONFLICTS.shareholders: USE 'more than 950' and cite the careers page. True under either figure so it cannot be contradicted. Do not use the 2019 figure of 938.
ADJUDICATED_CONFLICTS.employees: USE 'more than 1,300 skilled artisans, technicians, and aviation professionals' for narrative. If a total is needed, cite '1,523 Worldwide | 15 Statewide' explicitly attributed to the 2025 Top 49ers listing. DISCARD the SAM 'Fewer than 500' (a per-entity small-business size representation, not a headcount) and the LinkedIn figure.
ADJUDICATED_CONFLICTS.revenue: USE $341,146,301 (2024). The $13.8M aggregator figure is false and must never appear.
